title: Membrane structure (fluid mosaic); Diffusion and facilitated diffusion; Active transport, bulk transport and co-transport; Cell surface area and size limits
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MB02a#t2 term and clue written for the game; MB02a#t1 term and clue written for the game; MB02b#t2 term and clue written for the game; MB02b#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: MB01b#N.13, MB02a#N.7a, MB02b#N.3, MB04#N.3a, MB06#N.3a, MB02a#N.12, MB06#N.5, MB06#N.9, MB06#N.12.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Facilitated diffusion
items.clue: Passive net movement down a concentration gradient through a membrane protein.

items.label: Simple diffusion
items.clue: Passive movement of small non-polar molecules such as O₂ between the phospholipids.

items.label: Root hair cell
items.clue: Has a long extension giving a large surface area, with many carrier proteins for ions.

items.label: Alveolar epithelial cell
items.clue: Very thin, giving a short distance for gases to cross; together they form a huge surface.

questions.stem: A student claims that proteins in the plasma membrane can move sideways within the membrane. Which observation would best support this claim?

options.text: As the cell grows, the total amount of protein in its plasma membrane increases steadily.
When fluorescent proteins in one small patch are permanently bleached, the patch glows again within a minute.
Micrographs show proteins scattered among the phospholipids rather than forming a separate layer.
Proteins labelled on the outer surface of the plasma membrane are later found inside the cytosol.

questions.stem: A potassium channel in a cell membrane is open. Which statement describes the movement of ions through it?

options.text: Potassium ions diffuse through, down their gradient, with no ATP used.
Potassium ions and any other ions of similar size diffuse through the open pore.
Potassium ions are moved through in whichever direction the cell requires.
Potassium ions are carried through using energy from the hydrolysis of ATP.

questions.explanation: The channel gives one specific ion a hydrophilic route through the hydrophobic core. The ions move by facilitated diffusion, down their gradient, with no ATP.

questions.stem: An exchange surface changes: its surface area becomes 3 times as large, the difference in concentration across it becomes 2 times as large, and its thickness becomes 1.5 times as large. By what factor does the rate of diffusion change?

Root cells absorb nitrate ions from soil water in which the nitrate concentration is much lower than in the cell. When the roots are deprived of oxygen, nitrate uptake falls sharply. What explains these observations?

options.text: Nitrate is taken up by active transport in the same direction as diffusion but faster, and the lack of oxygen slows the diffusion.
Nitrate is taken up by pumps using ATP from aerobic respiration, so without oxygen the supply of ATP falls and active transport slows.
Nitrate is taken up by pumps using ATP already present in the cell, so removing oxygen must have affected the channel proteins instead.
Nitrate is taken up by facilitated diffusion through channels, which use ATP to move ions across against the gradient.

questions.stem: A cube of side 1 mm has a surface area of 6 mm², a volume of 1 mm³ and a surface area-to-volume ratio of 6. The side length is increased to 4 mm. What is the new surface area-to-volume ratio?

options.text: 6, because the surface area and the volume are both multiplied by four
1.5, because the area becomes 96 mm² and the volume becomes 64 mm³
24, because a larger cube has more surface, so the ratio rises fourfold
0.67, because it compares the 64 mm³ volume with the 96 mm² surface area

questions.explanation: Area = 6 × 4² = 96 mm²; volume = 4³ = 64 mm³; ratio = 96 ÷ 64 = 1.5. Area × 16, volume × 64: the ratio falls to a quarter.

questions.stem: A hypothetical toxin binds to and blocks all of the channel and transport proteins in the plasma membrane of a cell. Which prediction about the cell, immediately after exposure to the toxin, is best supported?

options.text: Its uptake of both glucose and O₂ will stop, since all substances cross through proteins.
Its glucose uptake will not change, since glucose passes freely through the phospholipid bilayer.
Its glucose uptake will rise through other routes to meet the cell's own need for glucose.
Its glucose uptake will fall sharply, while O₂ will still diffuse in across the bilayer.

questions.stem: A hypothetical single-celled organism has the shape of a rectangular solid, 20 μm long, 10 μm high and 10 μm wide. What is the cell's surface area-to-volume ratio?

Shrews are among the smallest mammals. Like larger mammals, they keep their body temperature nearly constant. A shrew must eat much more food per gram of its body mass each day than a deer does. Which statement best explains this difference?

options.text: A shrew's cells are much smaller than a deer's, so each has a higher SA:V and needs more food per gram.
A shrew's small body can store only a little heat, so it must eat often to refill that store.
A shrew uses more energy in total each day than a deer does, because its rate per gram of body mass is higher.
A shrew has a higher SA:V, so it loses heat faster per gram and needs more energy per gram to replace it.

questions.stem: A spherical single-celled organism grows from a radius of 10 µm to a radius of 30 µm, keeping its shape. Which prediction is best supported?

options.text: Its SA:V rises to three times the original, so each unit of volume is better supplied.
Its SA:V is unchanged, because its shape has not changed.
Its surface grows ninefold, so supply now easily exceeds its larger needs.
Its SA:V falls to one third, so less surface serves each unit of volume.

questions.explanation: SA:V goes from 0.30 to 0.10 µm⁻¹. Demand grows × 27; supply surface only × 9.
